newsitem.title: UK: Iraqi crude set to undermine Med sour crude market.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi crude set to undermine Med sour crude market.

text.p: With the first cargoes of Iraqi crude loading in Turkey and the Gulf on Monday, Mediterranean oil traders expected differentials for other sour grades to come under further pressure.
Prices for Russian Urals could fall to a 70-75 cent discount to Dated Brent from current levels of around Dated -30/-40, traders said.
"The main impact is on the most liquid sour which is Urals," said one trader. "Given the Urals differential to Brent today it has to come off further to be competitive."
A tanker left the Turkish port of Ceyhan on Monday carrying 153,000 tonnes of Iraqi Kirkuk crude purchased by Turkish state oil refiner Tupras.
Meanwhile, two vessels, one a VLCC, were being loaded with Iraqi crude at the northern Gulf Mina al-Bakr terminal, Gulf industry sources said on Monday.
Traders said that as Iraqi exports start to ramp up, buyers were shying away from other sour grades.
"We expect first (Iraqi) barrels soon...a one million barrel cargo of Kirkuk," said one trader for a major Mediterranean refiner. "Nobody wants to take positions on other grades."
Traders said that three or four small December-loading Urals cargoes and early January Iranian Light and Heavy cargoes were being quietly offered but bids were scarce.
